reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 09 and targeted source panel crop, complete unchanged external-02 2048x2048 raw RGBA and native face/frame/note/right-edge crops, full repair-agent white/cyan/alpha sheet and evidence, and unchanged naiwa.png; verified removal of both invented metal pins, restored plain frame/paper surfaces, retained small dark right-edge tab, two upper mark rows, hair, spectacles, uniform, collar, backing and transparency.

entries.positive_observation: Both previously invented circular metal pins are removed: the upper-left dark frame rail and upper cream paper are plain again, with no replacement fasteners. Native right-edge inspection confirms the original small dark tab remains as a compact edge protrusion. The note has TWO compact upper gray-mark rows and mostly blank lower paper, with no third row. Short light-grey brushed-back hair, high mildly receding hairline, cropped sides, short sideburns, thin grey eyebrows and fine wire-rim spectacles remain. The face has no moustache or beard and one serious closed mouth; the three-quarter left pose, gaze, crop and soft modeling remain. The dark olive uniform retains gold shoulder detailing, red pale/gold-trimmed collar patches and one dark-centered silver-white throat cross. The collar fits a short broad neck without a stalk, pinching or clipping. The complete dark tilted frame, opaque pale warm-grey backplate and cream note remain. Full white/cyan inspection shows a genuine transparent exterior with no visible interior holes, lost backing or working-matte ring.
entries.alpha_decision: Accept native RGBA extrema 0..254 after actual white/cyan/alpha inspection; no source-alpha replacement was performed or needed, and 252-254 values alone were not rejection grounds.
entries.visible_limitations: Fine spectacle rims, collar embroidery and note lettering are not reliably readable at 65x67; the review verifies visible frame/paper surfaces, hardware absence, tab shape and row count rather than transcribing glyphs or exact emblems.
